name: The Hypostasis of the Archons — Sophia, Veil, Rulers, Adam, Norea, Eleleth, and the Root Above
description: The tractate's whole disclosure: the blind ruler's claim, Adam and Eve and the rulers' pursuit, Norea's refusal, Eleleth's rescue and retrospective cosmology, Zoe and Sabaoth, and the promised ending still to come.

scenes.name: The arrogant ruler mistakes a local realm for the entirety
scenes.character: The chief ruler — blind, arrogant — declares himself sole god; a voice from incorruptibility names his error: he has mistaken absence from his field for absence from reality.

entities.name: Samael / Yaldabaoth — the blind chief ruler
"you are mistaken, Samael" — the voice from incorruptibility
his field's edge — no visible superior inside it

text.kicker: #1 · Nag Hammadi Codex II,4; Layton translation; Robinson's dating (before AD 350, attributed)
text.title: The arrogant ruler mistakes a local realm for the entirety
text.italic: The claim demonstrates the source-side operation: local power reads absence from its field as absence from reality, and claims total authority.

text.body: The tractate is a Gnostic exposition of the rulers' origin, nature and power. Their chief is blind, arrogant, and declares himself sole god; a voice from incorruptibility answers, naming the error: absence from his field is not absence from reality. The names Samael, Yaldabaoth, Saklas belong to the telling. It runs formation first, Norea's crisis, then Eleleth's retrospective disclosure — the late revelation changing how the earlier coercion reads.
Occurrences: the sole-god declaration and the voice's rebuke (#1); the three names (#1, #3); the field's edge as the claim's condition (#1, #3).

scenes.name: A formed human exceeds the makers
scenes.character: The rulers form Adam after an image they perceived; breath fails until spirit descends; the spiritual woman awakens Adam, escapes as a tree; the violated shadow stays in the narrative.

entities.name: Adam — formed after a perceived image; life exceeding their authority
spirit descending from the Adamantine Land
the spiritual woman — awakening Adam; escaping pursuit as a tree
the shadow — violated; materially necessary to Norea's later denial
the garden's prohibition; sleep becoming ignorance; expulsion and toil

text.kicker: #1 · the Genesis retelling in the consulted Layton telling
text.title: A formed human exceeds the makers
text.italic: The scene demonstrates the distinction between forming, naming and governing within a field, and originating the life that exceeds the jurisdiction claimed over it.

text.body: The rulers form Adam after an image they have perceived; the human becomes living through a power they do not own — breath fails until spirit descends from the Adamantine Land. The spiritual woman awakens Adam and escapes pursuit as a tree, leaving a shadow the rulers violate; expulsion and toil follow. Inability to originate life becomes an attempt to possess its manifestation; the woman/shadow distinction grounds Norea's later denial.
Occurrences: the formed Adam and the descending spirit (#1); the tree-escape (#1); the violated shadow (#1, grounding #2); the garden, sleep and expulsion (#1).

scenes.name: Norea refuses the ancestry of possession
scenes.character: The rulers claim her through Eve; she refuses the genealogy and names her origin above; their coercion is answered by her cry.

entities.name: Norea — daughter of Eve; refusing the imposed descent
the rulers' claim — authority through Eve; coercion attempted
her cry to the higher divine reality
the ark refused, breathed aflame — her relation to the flood set against Noah's

text.kicker: #2 · the flood and the refusal (q004's scope in the source house)
text.title: Norea refuses the ancestry of possession
text.italic: Her refusal demonstrates the contest at the level of origin: the rulers' claim to rule is contested not by stronger force but by recovered genealogy.

text.body: Cain farms; Abel keeps sheep; the offerings end in fratricide. Seth follows; Eve bears Norea. A ruler warns Noah; the ark rests on Mount Sir; Noah excludes Norea, whose breath burns it. When the rulers claim authority over her through Eve, she refuses the genealogy: she is not their descendant and comes from the world above. They attempt coercion; she cries to the higher reality for rescue.
Occurrences: the excluded Norea and the burnt ark (#2); the imposed genealogy and its refusal (#2); the cry (#2, answered at #3).

scenes.name: Eleleth: rescue and the rulers' own origin
scenes.character: The luminary rescues and teaches: Pistis Sophia's initiative, the veil, shadow, matter; the deficient ruler's second totalising claim; seven offspring and layered heavens; Zoe's rebuke; Sabaoth's change of allegiance.

entities.name: Eleleth — golden appearance, snowy clothing; rescue and disclosure
Pistis Sophia — desiring to create without her consort; the veil between worlds
shadow → matter → the lion-faced ruler — the second horizon-mistake
seven offspring and the layered heavens; Sabaoth in the seventh below the veil
Zoe's rebuke; Yaldabaoth bound in Tartaros; Sabaoth's throne and Zoe teaching at his right

text.kicker: #3 · the retrospective cosmology through Eleleth's revelation (q005's scope)
text.title: Eleleth: rescue and the rulers' own origin
text.italic: The revelation demonstrates the decisive operation: authority limited by recovered provenance — Norea receives an account of where the rulers came from, after they presumed to say where she came from.

text.body: Eleleth descends: he rescues Norea and teaches her her root and the rulers' own origin. Beneath the veil shadow becomes matter, and a lion-like ruler emerges. Seven offspring layer the heavens; Zoe's rebuke binds Yaldabaoth; Sabaoth sees the higher power, rejects his father, and is elevated in the seventh heaven — recognition within structure, not only escape. Sabaoth changes allegiance inside the genealogy; Norea denies it contains her root.

Occurrences: Eleleth's descent, appearance and teaching (#2–#3); the veil, shadow and matter (#3, compared at #4); the seven offspring and layered heavens (#3); Zoe's rebuke and Sabaoth's repentance (#3).

text.kicker: #4–#5→0 · the ending's bounded synopsis (Robinson); the Native 020 seam now owned; the human-amplified ledger
text.title: The root disclosed; the ending still to come
text.italic: The story's rulers are most dangerous not because they are unreal but because real local power is mistaken for self-grounding total authority — a system synthesis, human-amplified: no until ratified.

text.body: The revelation promises disclosure after three generations: the true Man will bring saving disclosure; the closing hymn gives the ending a collective voice. The deepest movement is false sovereignty corrected by provenance: the rulers' local world is real — their mistake is inferring from local efficacy that their order is self-grounding. Four system candidates stay human-amplified: no. The Valentinian whole remains distinct — Horos and Achamoth are not inserted here.

Occurrences: the refusal and the disclosure (#2–#3, #5→0); the promised ending (#4, #5→0). Declared cross-story: distinct from the Valentinian Sophia–Horos–Achamoth whole; no transmission asserted across the shared Sophia name.
